      hnarrow hcap (o := 11 * Real.pi / 8) (d := Real.pi) hpi.le Q
    refine ⟨q, hq, hQq, ?_, ?_⟩

        push_cast
        linarith
  · -- (true, false): fast positive, slow negative — difference near π

        push_cast
        linarith

      hnarrow hcap (o := 3 * Real.pi / 8) (d := 0) le_rfl Q

e the counterexample lives.

### 10.2 The Davenport–Heilbronn function is a counterexample `[FALSIFIES §7]`

Take the modulus `Q = 5`, `chi` the quartic character with `chi(2) = i`. The odd functions on
`Z/5` supported on the units are spanned by `chi` and `chi-bar`, so every FE eigenvector of that
parity is `alpha = (1, xi, -xi, -1, 0)` on residues `(1,2,3,4,0)` for a real `xi`, with
`alpha = c_1 chi + c_3 chi-bar`, `c_1 = (1 - i xi)/2`, `c_3 = (1 + i xi)/2`.

The eigenvector equations `-c_3 \bar u = eps c_1`, `c_1 u = eps c_3` with `u = tau(chi)/sqrt5` give
`eps^2 = -1`, i.e. `eps = ± i`, and

  `(1 - i xi)/(1 + i xi) = eps / u`,  hence  `xi = -tan(phi/2)`,  `e^{i phi} = eps / u`.

Both signs of `eps` occur. Replacing `eps` by `-eps` sends `phi` to `phi + pi` and hence
`xi = -tan(phi/2)` to `-1/xi`: the two resulting functions are the two Davenport–Heilbronn functions
with opposite root numbers, and their parameters are **reciprocal**, `xi' = -1/xi`.

Two exact facts are all that is needed, and no numerics enter.

- **`|xi| ≠ 1`.** `|xi| = |tan(phi/2)| = 1` iff `phi ≡ ± pi/2 (mod 2 pi)`, iff `e^{i phi} = ± i`,
  iff `eps/u = ± i`, iff `u = ± 1` (as `eps = ± i`), iff the Gauss sum `tau(chi)` is real. But
  `tau(chi) = sum_{n=1}^{4} chi(n) e(n/5) = -2 sin(4 pi/5) + 2 i sin(2 pi/5)` has imaginary part
  `2 sin(2 pi/5) ≠ 0`. So `|xi| ≠ 1`.
- **Exactly one branch has `|xi| > 1`**, since the two parameters are `xi` and `-1/xi` and
  `|xi| ≠ 1`.

Also `xi` is real (`phi` is real), and `alpha` is not multiplicative: `alpha(2)^2 = xi^2 >= 0` while
`alpha(4) = -1`. By Saias–Weingartner both branches therefore have infinitely many zeros with
`sigma > 1`.

Now take the branch with `|xi| > 1` and compute the local polynomials.

| `p mod 5` | `d` | `N_p(X)` | roots | reciprocal roots | `B_p` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `1` | 1 | `1` | none | none | `{log p}` finite |
| `2` | 4 | `(1-X^2)(1+xi X)` | `±1, -1/xi` | `1, -1, -xi` | `pi_k → ∞`, **discrete** |
| `3` | 4 | `(1-X^2)(1-xi X)` | `±1, 1/xi` | `1, -1, xi` | `pi_k → ∞`, **discrete** |
| `4` | 2 | `1 - X` | `1` | `1` | `{± log p}` finite |
| `p = 5` | — | `alpha(5^i) = 0` for `i>=1` | — | — | `{0}` |

Since `|xi| > 1`, the root `∓1/xi` lies strictly **inside** the unit disc, so the reciprocal root
`∓xi` has modulus `> 1` and is the unique dominant one; hence `|pi_k| → ∞` and `B_p` is discrete for
every prime. By §9.2–9.3 every fixed slice of the composite coefficients has poles only at roots of
`N_p`, so it also grows or vanishes; and for the mixed case `p ≡ 2`, `r ≡ 4` one has the exact
closed form

  `c_{p^i r^j} = ((-1)^{j+1}/j) · [X^i] (M_1/N_p)^j`,  `N_{p,r}(X,Y) = N_p(X) + Y M_1(X)`,

with `M_1` the two-step cyclic shift of `N_p`'s coefficient vector; because `|M_1(0)| = |alpha(4)| =
1` and `N_p` has a root inside the unit disc, these grow in `i` and are only polynomially controlled
in `j` — no exponential decay, hence no accumulation.

> **`[FALSIFIED]`** The conjecture of §7 is false. There is a degree-one element of the extended
> Selberg class with a zeta-type functional equation, **without** an Euler product, whose
> logarithmic-derivative coefficient set `{b_n}` is discrete — and which has infinitely many zeros
> with `sigma > 1`, hence very far off the critical line.

This **answers the immediate finite task** posed in
`euler-defect-controls-displacement.md`: *"Constructing or excluding such an `L` is the immediate
finite task."* The object exists. Discreteness of the value set of `{b_n}` is therefore **not** the
discontinuous invariant behind "Euler product ⟹ RH".

### 10.3 The repaired invariant

What Davenport–Heilbronn violates is not discreteness but **per-prime finiteness**, equivalently
(Theorem 2) the cyclotomic condition. So the corrected statement is:

> **[CONJECTURE — Local torsion rigidity in degree one]** Let `F` be a degree-one element of the
> extended Selberg class with `a_1(F) = 1`. If for **every** prime `p` the set
> `{b_{p^k} : k >= 1}` is *finite*, then `F(s) = L(s, chi)` for a Dirichlet character `chi`.

By Theorems 1–2 this is exactly the `[OPEN CORE]` of §7 (all `N_p` cyclotomic + FE ⟹ character),
now with the hypothesis stated at the right strength, and with Davenport–Heilbronn no longer a
threat: its `N_p` at `p ≡ 2, 3 (mod 5)` has the non-torsion root `∓1/xi`, so its `B_p` is infinite.

The invariant is now sharply **two-tiered**, and the tiers are exactly the two classical local
conditions:

- `|r| >= 1` for every root of `N_p` — the local **Ramanujan** condition. Davenport–Heilbronn
  *violates* this at `p ≡ 2, 3 (mod 5)` for the branch `|xi| > 1`, and violates the reflected
  condition for the branch `|xi| < 1`. So a Ramanujan-type bound is precisely what excludes
  Davenport–Heilbronn, and Selberg's class `S` imposes it as an axiom.
- **torsion** of the roots on top of Ramanujan — the Euler product itself.

So the correct slogan is not "multiplicativity is discreteness" but:

isons — including the ladders I built this month — are not merely
hard to close; by this analysis they are the wrong shape.

## §16 The additivity conjecture is RETRACTED — tested and falsified

§15 conjectured that no RH proof can come from a criterion in which the functional equation and the
Euler product appear as separate additive terms.  I tested it two ways.  It fails both.

**Test 1 — the classification.**  Kaczorowski–Perelli (*On the structure of the Selberg class, I:
0 ≤ d ≤ 1*, Acta Math. 182 (1999)) classify the degree-one elements of the Selberg class: they are
exactly `zeta` and the shifted Dirichlet `L`-functions.  So the *joint* hypothesis — functional
equation with Gamma-factor, Euler product, Ramanujan bound, degree one — **has no counterexample
family at all.**  There is no "Davenport–Heilbronn with an Euler product" and no
"Diamond–Montgomery–Vorhauer with a Gamma-factor functional equation": the two no-go families of §14

## Proof

[PROVED HERE]

Work in seam coordinates `w=s-1/2` and reciprocal coordinate

```text
y = -1/w^2.
```

An FE-symmetric, real-conjugation-symmetric off-line quartet has points

```text
w in { a+i gamma, -a+i gamma, a-i gamma, -a-i gamma },
```

with `a>0` and `gamma>0`. Define

```text
T_k = sum_{quartet} y^k.
```

Direct algebra gives

```text
det [[T_1,T_2],[T_2,T_3]]
  = -64 a^2 gamma^2 / (a^2+gamma^2)^6,
```

and

```text
det [[T_2,T_3],[T_3,T_4]]
  = -64 a^2 gamma^2 / (a^2+gamma^2)^8.
```

Both determinants are strictly negative when `a gamma != 0`. Therefore the degree-one shifted blocks

```text
H_1^(0) = [T_{i+j+1}]_{i,j=0}^1,
H_1^(1) = [T_{i+j+2}]_{i,j=0}^1
```

are not PSD for an off-line quartet.

At `a=0`, the quartet collapses to duplicated on-line conjugate points. Then `y=1/gamma^2` is positive and the same determinants vanish, giving the expected rank-one PSD boundary case.

/-!
# The pre-spectral firewall as an explicit genuine/fake separation

`EulerProduct` proves the First Theorem (`isMultiplicative_iff_bohr_factorization`) and, separately,
that the Davenport–Heilbronn-style fake coefficient is not multiplicative
(`davenportHeilbronnFakeCoeff_not_isMultiplicative`).  This file composes them into the single
separation the firewall is about: every genuine (multiplicative) Dirichlet coefficient Bohr-factors
over the primes, while the fake fails to — witnessed at a finite `n`, before any zero is examined.
-/

open scoped BigOperators
open ArithmeticFunction

namespace GaloisForLFunctions

/-- **The pre-spectral firewall, as a separation.**  For every genuine (multiplicative) Dirichlet
coefficient function `f`, the Bohr lift factors over the primes at every `n`; yet the
Davenport–Heilbronn-style fake coefficient fails that factorization at some finite `n`.  The Euler
product / Bohr factorization property separates the genuine from the fake, pre-spectrally — no zero is
examined. -/
theorem euler_firewall_separation {f : ArithmeticFunction ℂ} (hf : f.IsMultiplicative) :
    (∀ n : ℕ, n ≠ 0 → f n = n.factorization.prod fun p k => f (p ^ k))
    ∧ (∃ n : ℕ, n ≠ 0 ∧
        davenportHeilbronnFakeCoeff n
          ≠ n.factorization.prod fun p k => davenportHeilbronnFakeCoeff (p ^ k)) :=
  ⟨((isMultiplicative_iff_bohr_factorization f).mp hf).2,
    fake_fails_factorization davenportHeilbronnFakeCoeff
      (by unfold davenportHeilbronnFakeCoeff; norm_num [davenportHeilbronnFakeCoeffInt])
      davenportHeilbronnFakeCoeff_not_isMultiplicative⟩

end GaloisForLFunctions

import GaloisForLFunctions.Core

/-!
# The field's First Theorem: Euler product ⟺ Bohr-lift factorization (Tier A)

`hypertranscendental_galois_field_foundations.md` §9 ("the field's FIRST THEOREM"):
a Dirichlet series `D(s) = Σ aₙ n^{-s}` has an **Euler product** iff its **Bohr lift
factors over the prime coordinates** iff it is a single irreducible tensor difference
module. The pre-spectral firewall: a series with no Euler product (a non-multiplicative
`aₙ`) does not factor, and this is detectable at a finite `n` — *before any zero is
examined*. The known fakes (Davenport–Heilbronn, Epstein) are non-multiplicative and so
fall on the wrong side of this dichotomy.

Here the Dirichlet coefficients are modelled by `ArithmeticFunction ℂ` (`ℕ → ℂ` with
`a 0 = 0`, `a 1 = 1` the normalization), and "Bohr lift factors over primes" is exactly
the multiplicative factorization `aₙ = ∏_{p ∣ n} a(p^{vₚ(n)})`.

* `isMultiplicative_iff_bohr_factorization` — the First Theorem (both directions).
  The forward direction is mathlib's `IsMultiplicative.multiplicative_factorization`; the
  converse (factorization ⟹ multiplicative) is the new content, via disjointness of the
  prime supports for coprime arguments (`Finsupp.prod_add_index_of_disjoint`).
* `fake_fails_factorization` — the firewall: a normalized non-multiplicative series fails
  the prime factorization at some finite `n` (no Euler product, witnessed pre-spectrally).

This is rigorous and pre-spectral. It encodes no zero, no positivity, no RH. The
representation-theoretic spine ("irreducible ⟺ Euler product ⟺ maximal `G_L`-orbit") and
its conjectural consequence (DSS/RH) are NOT formalized and remain frontier statements.
-/

open scoped BigOperators

open ArithmeticFunction

namespace GaloisForLFunctions

noncomputable section

/-- **The field's First Theorem (Euler product ⟺ Bohr-lift factorization).**
A Dirichlet coefficient function `f` is multiplicative (has an Euler product) iff it is
normalized `f 1 = 1` and its Bohr lift factors over the prime coordinates, i.e.
`f n = ∏_{p ∣ n} f (p ^ vₚ(n))` for every `n ≠ 0`. -/
@[aesop norm simp]
theorem isMultiplicative_iff_bohr_factorization (f : ArithmeticFunction ℂ) :
    f.IsMultiplicative ↔
      (f 1 = 1 ∧ ∀ n : ℕ, n ≠ 0 → f n = n.factorization.prod fun p k => f (p ^ k)) := by
  constructor
  · intro hf
    exact ⟨hf.map_one, fun n hn =>
      ArithmeticFunction.IsMultiplicative.multiplicative_factorization f hf hn⟩
  · rintro ⟨h1, hfact⟩
    rw [ArithmeticFunction.IsMultiplicative.iff_ne_zero]
    refine ⟨h1, ?_⟩
    intro m n hm hn hcop
    have hdisj : Disjoint m.factorization.support n.factorization.support := by
      rw [Nat.support_factorization, Nat.support_factorization]
      exact hcop.disjoint_primeFactors
    rw [hfact (m * n) (Nat.mul_ne_zero hm hn), hfact m hm, hfact n hn,
        Nat.factorization_mul hm hn, Finsupp.prod_add_index_of_disjoint hdisj]

/-- **The pre-spectral firewall.** A normalized (`f 1 = 1`) Dirichlet series with **no
Euler product** (non-multiplicative `f`) fails the prime factorization at some finite `n`:
there is `n ≠ 0` with `f n ≠ ∏_{p ∣ n} f (p ^ vₚ(n))`. The failure of the Euler product is
witnessed at a finite `n`, before any zero is examined — the fake-family obstruction made
intrinsic and pre-spectral. -/
@[aesop safe]
theorem fake_fails_factorization (f : ArithmeticFunction ℂ)
    (h1 : f 1 = 1) (hnm : ¬ f.IsMultiplicative) :
    ∃ n : ℕ, n ≠ 0 ∧ f n ≠ n.factorization.prod fun p k => f (p ^ k) := by
  by_contra h
  push Not at h
  exact hnm ((isMultiplicative_iff_bohr_factorization f).mpr ⟨h1, h⟩)

/-- The real part of the primitive order-4 Dirichlet character modulo `5`, as used
in the Davenport-Heilbronn-style fake-family witness: residues `1,4` have real
parts `1,-1`, and residues `0,2,3` have real part `0`. -/
def davenportHeilbronnFakeCoeffInt (n : ℕ) : ℤ :=
  match n % 5 with
  | 1 => 1
  | 4 => -1
  | _ => 0

/-- The corresponding normalized arithmetic-function coefficient model over `ℂ`.
This is only the finite coefficient firewall witness, not a formalization of the
Davenport-Heilbronn function, its functional equation, or its zeros. -/
def davenportHeilbronnFakeCoeff : ArithmeticFunction ℂ :=
  ZeroHom.mk (fun n => (davenportHeilbronnFakeCoeffInt n : ℂ)) (by
    norm_num [davenportHeilbronnFakeCoeffInt])

/-- **Concrete fake-family firewall witness.** The mod-5 Davenport-Heilbronn-style
coefficient model is not multiplicative: `a_6 = 1` but `a_2 a_3 = 0`. This is the
finite, pre-spectral obstruction behind the chat computation; it examines no zeros
and proves no RH/GRH localization statement. -/
@[aesop safe]
theorem davenportHeilbronnFakeCoeff_not_isMultiplicative :
    ¬ davenportHeilbronnFakeCoeff.IsMultiplicative := by
  intro hmul
  have h23 : davenportHeilbronnFakeCoeff (2 * 3)
      = davenportHeilbronnFakeCoeff 2 * davenportHeilbronnFakeCoeff 3 :=
    hmul.2 (by norm_num : Nat.Coprime 2 3)

hexp_ratio : Complex.exp (h₁ p - h₂ p) = H₁ p / H₂ p := by
      rw [Complex.exp_sub, hexp₁ p hp₁, hexp₂ p hp₂]
    rcases root_ratio_pm_one (hpH₁ p hp₁) (hpH₂ p hp₂) hf with hρ | hρ
    · obtain ⟨m, hm⟩ := im_eq_int_mul_pi_of_exp_real (r := 1) one_ne_zero
        (by rw [hexp_ratio, hρ]; norm_num)
      refine ⟨m, hm, ?_⟩
      have hre : (h₁ p - h₂ p).re = 0 := by
        have hnorm := congrArg norm hexp_ratio
        rw [Complex.norm_exp, hρ, norm_one] at hnorm
        exact Real.exp_injective (by rw [hnorm, Real.exp_zero])
      have hw : h₁ p - h₂ p = ((m * Real.pi : ℝ) : ℂ) * I := by
        apply Complex.ext
        · simp [hre]
        · simp [hm]
      rw [← hexp_ratio, hw,
        show ((m * Real.pi : ℝ) : ℂ) * I = (m : ℂ) * (Real.pi * I) from by
          push_cast; ring,
        Complex.exp_int_mul, Complex.exp_pi_mul_I]
    · obtain ⟨m, hm⟩ := im_eq_int_mul_pi_of_exp_real (r := -1)
        (by norm_num)
        (by rw [hexp_ratio, hρ]; norm_num)
      refine ⟨m, hm, ?_⟩
      have hre : (h₁ p - h₂ p).re = 0 := by
        have hnorm := congrArg norm hexp_ratio
        rw [Complex.norm_exp, hρ, norm_neg, norm_one] at hnorm
        exact Real.exp_injective (by rw [hnorm, Real.exp_zero])
      have hw : h₁ p - h₂ p = ((m * Real.pi : ℝ) : ℂ) * I := by
        apply Complex.ext
        · simp [hre]
        · simp [hm]
      rw [← hexp_ratio, hw,
        show ((m * Real.pi : ℝ) : ℂ) * I = (m : ℂ) * (Real.pi * I) from by
          push_cast; ring,
        Complex.exp_int_mul, Complex.exp_pi_mul_I]
  obtain ⟨mP, hmP, hρP⟩ := key pP hpP₁ hpP₂ hfP
  obtain ⟨mM, hmM, hρM⟩ := key pM hpM₁ hpM₂ hfM
  refine ⟨mP, mM, hmP, hmM, ?_⟩
  rw [deckClass, hρP, hρM, ← zpow_sub₀ (by norm_num : (-1 : ℂ) ≠ 0)]

/-! ### §5 The discriminator: frozen without the Euler head, dense with it -/

/-- The empty anchor has zero canonical logarithm. -/
theorem anchorLog_empty (s : ℂ) : anchorLog ∅ s = 0 := by
  rw [anchorLog, Finset.sum_empty]

/-- **The anchor-free sweep is constant** — the formal shadow of a functional
equation without an Euler product: nothing to sweep, every boundary reading
frozen.  This is the Davenport–Heilbronn side of the discriminator. -/
theorem anchorSweep_empty (t : ℝ) (s : ℂ) : anchorSweep ∅ t s = 1 := by
  rw [anchorSweep, anchorLog_empty]
  norm_num

/-- The anchor-free root transport is the identity. -/
theorem sweepRoot_empty (t : ℝ) (H : ℂ → ℂ) (z : ℂ) :
    sweepRoot ∅ t H z = H z := by
  rw [sweepRoot, anchorLog_empty]
  norm_num

/-- **The Euler side of the discriminator**: the sweep-holonomy pair — half the
anchor tilts at the two basepoints, the exact angles the two basepoint root
readings turn under the full sweep — reaches every nonnegative target box within
every tolerance, over prime sets beyond any bound.  The Euler walk couples to the
square-root sheet densely; the empty anchor not at all. -/
theorem sweep_holonomy_pair_reachable {ρ : ℂ} {c : ℝ}
    (hre0 : 0 < ρ.re) (hre1 : ρ.re < 1)
    (hc : 0 < c) (hcτ : c < ρ.im)
    (hnarrow : 9 * (2 * c) ≤ ρ.im + c)
    (hcap : (ρ.im + c) * (4 * Real.log 2) < Real.pi)
    {Tp Tm : ℝ} (hTp : 0 ≤ Tp) (hTm : 0 ≤ Tm) {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) (Q : ℕ) :
    ∃ P : Finset ℕ, (∀ p ∈ P, Nat.Prime p ∧ Q < p) ∧
      |Tp - anchorTilt P (ρ + (c : ℂ) * I) / 2| ≤ ε ∧
      |Tm - anchorTilt P (ρ - (c : ℂ) * I) / 2| ≤ ε := by
  obtain ⟨P, hP, hp, hm⟩ := anchorTilt_pair_reachable_nonneg hre0 hre1 hc hcτ
    hnarrow hcap (Tp := 2 * Tp) (Tm := 2 * Tm) (by linarith) (by linarith)
    (ε := 2 * ε) (by linarith) Q
  refine ⟨P, hP, ?_, ?_⟩
  · rw [abs_le] at hp ⊢
    constructor <;> [linarith [hp.1]; linarith [hp.2]]
  · rw [abs_le] at hm ⊢
    constructor <;> [linarith [hm.1]; linarith [hm.2]]

/-- The sweep preserves the analytic order at every strip point: the homotopy from
the member to the anchored member never moves a zero or changes its multiplicity —
the hole count is a sweep invariant. -/
theorem analyticOrderAt_anchorSweep_mul {P : Finset ℕ} (hP : ∀ p ∈ P, 2 ≤ p)
    (t : ℝ) {f : ℂ → ℂ} {z : ℂ} (hf : AnalyticAt ℂ f z) (hz : 0 < z.re) :
    analyticOrderAt (fun w => anchorSweep P t w * f w) z = analyticOrderAt f z := by
  have hA : AnalyticAt ℂ (anchorSweep P t) z := anchorSweep_analyticAt hP t hz
  have hfun : (fun w => anchorSweep P t w * f w) = anchorSweep P t * f := rfl
  rw [hfun, analyticOrderAt_mul hA hf,
    hA.analyticOrderAt_eq_zero.mpr (anchorSweep_ne_zero P t z), zero_add]

/-- **The discriminator's observable**: the full sweep multiplies the
cross-basepoint root ratio by a positive scalar and the rotation by HALF the
endpoint tilt difference — the relative sweep holonomy.  The scalar is
parity-blind; the rotation is the steerable reading. -/
theorem sweepRoot_cross_ratio (P : Finset ℕ) (H : ℂ → ℂ) (pP pM : ℂ) :
    sweepRoot P 1 H pP / sweepRoot P 1 H pM
      = ((Real.exp (((anchorLog P pP).re - (anchorLog P pM).re) / 2) : ℝ) : ℂ)
        * (Complex.exp ((((anchorTilt P pP - anchorTilt P pM) / 2 : ℝ) : ℂ) * I)
            * (H pP / H pM)) := by

/-
The quadratic (Arf) face of the seam's `J`-collapse.

Two earlier faces record how the functional equation's conjugate-pairing of zeros — the
reflection involution `σ` (`J`) — annihilates every mod-2 shadow of the winding index:

* the **real** face (`SeamNullConeSignature`): the polarized seam form has inertia triple
  `(sigPos, sigNeg, dim radical) = (even, even, even)` — neutral, never Lorentzian;
* the **linear** face (`SignatureParity`): the deck class at `n = 2` is the reduction
  homomorphism `ℤ → ZMod 2`, and a fixed-point-free multiplicity-matching involution puts
  the reflection-paired zeros (and the ramified fixed point) entirely in its kernel.

This file is the **quadratic** face.  The reflection matching is a perfect matching of the
off-line zeros — a nondegenerate *alternating* `ZMod 2`-form whose symplectic planes are the
conjugate pairs `{ρ, σ ρ}`, the only `ZMod 2` symplectic structure the boundary data carries.
Its **Arf invariant** is the sum of the plane densities `q ρ * q (σ ρ)` over a conjugate-pair
transversal — the one genuinely-quadratic bit one could hope reads more than the linear deck
parity.  It does not:

    `q ρ * q (σ ρ) = q ρ`   **pointwise** on the matched set,

because a reflection-*equivariant* refinement satisfies `q (σ ρ) = q ρ` and `x * x = x` in
`ZMod 2`.  So the Arf density equals the linear deck density term by term; the Arf invariant
collapses to `∑ q ρ` over the transversal — a *linear* functional of the deck data, carrying
nothing beyond it — and over the whole matched set it is `0` (the linear face again).

The single escape — a refinement with `q (σ ρ) ≠ q ρ` — uses data not invariant under
conjugation, i.e. a choice of branch of `√ξ`, a section of the deck cover: a flow, not a
constraint, hence not seam-canonical.  Externally, a functional equation with simple off-line
zeros (Davenport–Heilbronn) shows no functional-equation-canonical invariant of any degree can
force off-line parity, so the collapse is the true state, not an artifact of this refinement.

No higher-degree escape exists either: the reflection matching is `ZMod 2`-valued, so it
supports a `ZMod 2` (Arf) refinement only — there is no `ZMod 4` symplectic form on the
boundary data to carry a Brown-type invariant.  The deck classes at every level `n = 2^k` are
the *linear* reduction homomorphism (`SignatureParity`); the quadratic refinement exists only
at `k = 1`, and it collapses here.
-/
import GaloisForLFunctions.RHTower.SignatureParity
import GaloisForLFunctions.RHTower.Reflection

open scoped BigOperators

open Complex

namespace RHTower

/-! ### §1 Idempotence in `ZMod 2` -/

/-- In `ZMod 2` every element is idempotent: `x * x = x`.  This is the whole reason a
reflection-equivariant quadratic refinement has no quadratic content — the plane density
`q e * q (σ e) = q e * q e = q e`. -/
theorem zmod2_mul_self (x : ZMod 2) : x * x = x := by revert x; decide

/-! ### §2 The abstract Arf collapse

`σ : ι → ι` is the reflection matching of the index set; `q : ι → ZMod 2` is a refinement
(a `ZMod 2`-value at each index).  "Reflection-equivariant" means `q (σ i) = q i` — the datum
is invariant under conjugation, as any germ-local invariant of ξ automatically is. -/

/-- **Arf density = linear density, pointwise.**  For a reflection-equivariant refinement `q`
(`q (σ i) = q i` on `s`) the quadratic Arf density `q i * q (σ i)` equals the linear deck
density `q i` at every matched index: the genuinely-quadratic content is empty. -/
theorem arfDensity_eq_linear {ι : Type*} (σ : ι → ι) (q : ι → ZMod 2) {s : Finset ι}
    (hq : ∀ i ∈ s, q (σ i) = q i) : ∀ i ∈ s, q i * q (σ i) = q i := by
  intro i hi
  rw [hq i hi]
  exact zmod2_mul_self (q i)

/-- **The Arf invariant collapses to the linear deck sum.**  Over any index set on which `q`
is reflection-equivariant, the Arf sum `∑ q i * q (σ i)` equals the linear sum `∑ q i`.  Taken
over a conjugate-pair transversal the left side is the Arf invariant of the reflection
matching, so the Arf invariant is a *linear* functional of the deck parities — it reads
nothing the linear deck class does not. -/
theorem arf_sum_eq_linear_sum {ι : Type*} (σ : ι → ι) (q : ι → ZMod 2) (s : Finset ι)
    (hq : ∀ i ∈ s, q (σ i) = q i) :
    ∑ i ∈ s, q i * q (σ i) = ∑ i ∈ s, q i :=
  Finset.sum_congr rfl (arfDensity_eq_linear σ q hq)

/-- **The Arf invariant is representative-independent.**  Because `q (σ i) = q i`, replacing a
conjugate-pair representative `i` by its partner `σ i` does not change its deck parity, so the
transversal sum `∑ q i` — the Arf invariant — does not depend on which member of each pair is
chosen.  Equivariance alone makes the invariant well defined; no symplectic-basis choice is
needed and none of the classical Arf well-definedness machinery is invoked. -/
theorem arf_repr_indep {ι : Type*} (σ : ι → ι) (q : ι → ZMod 2)
    (hq : ∀ i, q (σ i) = q i) (i : ι) : q (σ i) = q i := hq i

/-
The tilt-sweep discriminator: the Euler anchor couples to the parity sheet at half
rate; an anchor-free member has no sweep at all.

The finite Euler head admits the canonical power family `A^t = exp(t·anchorLog)` —
